facts.text: University Heights is a city in Johnson County, Iowa, and part of the Iowa City Metropolitan Statistical Area.
The town sits as an enclave surrounded by Iowa City, just a stone's throw from the University of Iowa campus.
University Heights' city border lies only about 0.1 miles from Kinnick Stadium, the University of Iowa’s football arena.
Before becoming a city, the area was West Lucas Township, a patchwork of small farms and properties in the early 1900s.
In the early 1920s, brothers Lee and George Koser began buying and developing land that would become University Heights, foreseeing the university’s westward growth.
All 241 lots in the original subdivisions carried racially restrictive covenants that were legally enforceable until the 1948 Supreme Court Shelley v. Kraemer decision.
